subject: Day 68: swiping at the play gym
bodyText:
Today's focus
Reaching is shifting from accidental to deliberate. Today is about giving Avi a play gym set up so his swipes at hanging toys turn into purposeful, repeatable practice.

Action items
- Hang two or three toys at swat height on the play gym so his arms make contact when he reaches; deliberate batting at this age builds the reach-and-grasp foundation that consolidates over the next couple of months. AAP HealthyChildren: movement, birth to 3 months: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-Birth-to-Three-Months.aspx
- Rotate the toys you hang every few days so the visual and motor targets stay novel rather than ignored. AAP HealthyChildren: baby senses: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/default.aspx
- Keep total container time (bouncer, swing, car seat outside the car) under 2 hours per day so floor and play-gym time stays the default.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Non-painful spit-up and frequent hand-sucking during play; both are routine at this stage.
- [monitor] Movement that consistently favors one side, or hands that stay fisted without occasionally opening; note it for the next visit.
- [call within 24h] A feeding refusal lasting more than 24 hours, or a new persistent crying pattern with no clear trigger.
- [call now] Rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher, sudden limpness, apnea, or blue lips with labored breathing. Call 911 right away for blue lips!

Enrichment opportunities
- Hang toys at swat height on the play gym and let him practice deliberate reaching and swiping; this is the motor work that bridges into grasping. AAP HealthyChildren: movement, birth to 3 months: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-Birth-to-Three-Months.aspx
- Set a toy swinging and let him track it; vary the colors and shapes you hang to keep his fluid visual tracking engaged. AAP HealthyChildren: baby senses: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/default.aspx
- Narrate his hits and misses in real time (you got it, almost, try again) so the language stream stays tied to what his body is doing. Romeo et al. 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/

Upcoming
- Day 84-91: sleep-consolidation window opens around 3 months; keep the wind-down routine steady.
- Day 112-126: 4-month well visit and vaccines (RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2).
- Around week 14-18: 4-month sleep regression on the horizon; reaching and rolling often emerge alongside it.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Smiles on his own to get your attention
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Initiates the smile rather than responding to yours — emerging social agency.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/smiles-to-get-attention/complete

- Chuckles (not yet a full laugh)
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Throaty soft laugh sounds. Precedes the full belly laugh by a few weeks.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/chuckles/complete

- Turns head toward the sound of your voice
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Localizes sound source. Worth raising with the pediatrician if absent at the 4-month visit.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/turns-head-toward-sound/complete

- Makes sounds back when you talk to him
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Conversational turn-taking. Foundation for later vocabulary growth.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/makes-sounds-back/complete

- Opens mouth when she sees the breast or bottle
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Anticipatory recognition — feeding is now associated with the sight, not just the sensation.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/opens-mouth-for-breast/complete
